title: True certainty needs solid object-ground and right apprehension
source_text: V. Ad veri nominis autem certitudinem menti ingenerandam requiritur ex parte objecti fundamentum aliquod solidum quo intellectus innitatur: ac praeterea ut vim & soliditatem ejus mens rite apprehendat, eique objectum tale quale est videatur. Nam aliquando contingit, ex ingenii tarditate aut mentis praejudicio, ut vim & lucem objecti mens non satis percipiat, ac proinde levem tantum concipiat persuasionem rei illius, de qua tamen nullus est haerendi & dubitandi locus.
pass_a_gloss: But for generating true-name certainty in the mind there is required on the object’s side some solid foundation on which the intellect rests: and moreover that the mind rightly apprehend its force and solidity, and that the object appear to it such as it is. For sometimes it happens, from sluggishness of wit or prejudice of mind, that the mind does not sufficiently perceive the force and light of the object, and therefore conceives only a light persuasion of that thing concerning which yet there is no place for sticking and doubting.
pass_b_english: True certitudo needs solid object-foundation for the intellect.
Mind must rightly grasp that solidity — object as it is.
Sluggishness/prejudice → only light persuasion where doubt has no place.
